justify_why_gaps_are_missing.justification: x-axis represents binned Pol II ChIP-seq signal across a continuous gradient with no skipped ranges or abrupt repositioning; visual spacing is continuous so no axis break is required.
y-axis shows percent state frequency from 0 to 100 with regularly spaced ticks and a continuous stacked area—no omitted interval or discontinuity that would require a break marker.
x-axis is position relative to TSS spanning -200 to +200 bp with continuous coordinate ticks and no omitted intervals.
y-axis is an index of molecules (ordinal) shown continuously (no skipped ranges); there is no indication of omitted rows or a compressed region requiring a break symbol.
x-axis represents binned Pol II ChIP-seq levels across a continuous gradient analogous to panel A; no skipped numeric ranges or visual discontinuities are present.
y-axis shows percent state frequency (0–100) with evenly spaced ticks and continuous stacked areas; no omitted interval requiring a break.
x-axis is continuous genomic position relative to TSS (-200 to +200 bp) with no omitted segments or compressed ranges; no break is required.
y-axis is a continuous listing of single molecules (ordinal scale) with no apparent skipped rows or compressed region that would warrant an axis break indicator.
x-axis lists categorical groups (TATA-less, TATA for two species); categorical axes do not require numeric breaks.
y-axis shows PIC occupancy (%) with regularly spaced tick marks and continuous numeric scale; there are no large skipped ranges or abrupt jumps that would require a break label.
x-axis is categorical (group labels) and continuous spacing is appropriate; no axis break concept applies.
y-axis shows Pol II occupancy (%) with continuous numeric scale and evenly spaced ticks; no omitted numeric intervals or compressed regions are evident that would require an axis break marker.
